_comment: Access Control Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor — mirrors cm.json structure with AC-domain content. Add new families by copying this file (or cm.json) and replacing the family-specific fields.
title: Access Control Plan
description: Documents how the organization controls who can access the system, what they can do once authenticated, and how that access is reviewed and revoked. Covers the controls of the AC family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-63 (Digital Identity Guidelines) and NIST SP 800-162 (ABAC).
intro_template:
This Access Control Plan documents the access-control approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, roles, and technical mechanisms used to enforce who may access the system and at what level of privilege.

The scope covers identity sources, account lifecycle, access enforcement, privileged access, session management, remote and wireless access, and external system connections within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Access Control family), NIST SP 800-63 (Digital Identity Guidelines), and where applicable NIST SP 800-162 (Attribute-Based Access Control).
approach_template:
{system_name} relies on {iam_tool} as the identity and access management system of record. Access decisions are enforced via {access_enforcement_model}. The account lifecycle (joiner / mover / leaver) is processed via {account_workflow}. Privileged access is governed through {pam_approach}.

Additional details on identity management, access enforcement, privileged access, session management, remote / wireless access, and external system connections are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Account inventories, privilege assignments, and active sessions for {system_name} are reviewed on a defined cadence and reconciled against authoritative HR / personnel records. Dormant accounts are identified and either disabled or removed per the account-review process. Privileged access is recertified periodically and just-in-time grants are logged for audit. Remote-access usage and authentication failures feed the SIEM. Continuous-monitoring metrics related to AC controls are documented in the sub-sections below.
integration_template: This Access Control Plan does not stand alone. Control implementations described herein are referenced from the System Security Plan (SSP); identity-related findings flow into the Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M); authentication failures and unauthorized-access events are logged for AU-2 / AU-12 audit collection and inform CA-7 continuous monitoring. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where AC-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Identity tooling, access-enforcement model, and the account lifecycle that everything else hangs off.

questions.label: Identity and access management system of record
questions.help: Authoritative identity source / IAM platform (e.g., Active Directory + Azure AD, Okta, AWS IAM, Keycloak).

questions.label: Access-enforcement model
questions.help: Primary access decision model. Most modern systems use RBAC or RBAC+ABAC.

questions.label: Account lifecycle workflow (joiner / mover / leaver)
questions.help: End-to-end JML workflow: how new accounts are requested, approved, provisioned, modified on role change, and deprovisioned on departure. Mention tooling (ServiceNow, ITSM, Okta workflows) and approval thresholds.

questions.label: Privileged access management (PAM) approach
questions.help: How privileged access is governed: standing privileges vs just-in-time, vault-based credential checkout, session recording, etc. Tooling (CyberArk, BeyondTrust, AWS SSO with permission sets, Teleport).

family_questions.label: Identity Management
family_questions.description: Identity sources, lifecycle, federation, and authoritative records.

questions.label: Authoritative identity source
questions.help: System of record for identity (e.g., 'Workday HR feeds Active Directory nightly').

questions.label: Federation partners (if any)
questions.help: External identity providers federated with the system. Add each via the Add button or pick from suggestions.

questions.label: User populations served
questions.help: Distinct populations the system authenticates. Each may have different controls applied.

questions.label: Identity proofing level (NIST SP 800-63A)
options: IAL2 (in-person or remote with verifiable evidence)
questions.help: Per NIST SP 800-63A. Most federal systems require IAL2; CUI/Secret often require IAL3.

questions.label: Authenticator assurance level (NIST SP 800-63B)
questions.help: Per NIST SP 800-63B. Federal systems handling CUI typically require AAL2; privileged or classified often AAL3.

family_questions.label: Access Enforcement
family_questions.description: How access decisions are made and enforced at the policy decision and enforcement points.

questions.label: Policy decision point (PDP)
questions.help: Component that evaluates access requests against policy (e.g., 'AWS IAM', 'OPA + Rego policies', 'Application authorization layer').

questions.label: Policy enforcement points (PEPs)
questions.help: Where decisions are enforced — load balancer, application middleware, OS-level (sudo / RBAC), database row-level security, etc.

questions.label: Role definitions / catalog
questions.help: Where roles are defined and reviewed (e.g., 'Roles documented in iam-roles repo; reviewed quarterly by ISSO + Engineering Lead').

questions.label: Attribute sources (for ABAC)
questions.help: If ABAC is in use, where attributes come from (HR system, IdP claims, classification labels) and how they're refreshed.

family_questions.label: Privileged Access
family_questions.description: PAM tooling, just-in-time access, separation of duties, and recertification.

questions.label: PAM tooling
questions.help: Privileged access management product / approach (e.g., CyberArk, BeyondTrust, AWS SSO permission sets, HashiCorp Vault, Teleport).

questions.label: Just-in-time access approach
questions.help: How elevated privileges are requested and time-bound. Standing-privilege exceptions, if any.

questions.label: Separation-of-duties enforcement
questions.help: How conflicting role pairs are prevented (e.g., 'Auditor and Production Deploy roles are mutually exclusive; enforced via Okta access policies').

questions.label: Privileged access recertification cadence
questions.help: How often privileged role membership is reviewed and recertified by the role owner.

family_questions.label: Session Management
family_questions.description: Idle timeouts, device locking, concurrent session limits.

questions.label: Idle timeout before lock
questions.help: Time of inactivity before automatic device lock or session termination (e.g., '15 minutes for non-privileged; 5 minutes for privileged').

questions.label: Lock mechanism
questions.help: How the lock is implemented (OS screen lock + session unlock requires re-authentication; web-app session timeout).

questions.label: Session termination triggers
questions.help: Conditions that terminate (not just lock) a session: idle threshold, explicit logout, security event detection, account disable.

questions.label: Concurrent session limits
questions.help: Whether and how concurrent sessions per account are limited (per role / per account-type).

family_questions.label: Remote, Wireless, and Mobile Access
family_questions.description: VPN / remote-access mechanisms, wireless policy, mobile device approach.

questions.label: Remote-access mechanisms
questions.help: How remote users connect (VPN, ZTNA, bastion host, SSH jump host) and what authentication is required (MFA, certificate, hardware token).

questions.label: Remote-access monitoring
questions.help: How remote-access sessions are logged and monitored (SIEM rule, anomaly detection).

questions.label: Wireless access policy
questions.help: Whether the system supports wireless access; if so, encryption requirements (WPA3 Enterprise), authentication, and segmentation.

questions.label: MDM / MAM tooling
questions.help: Tool managing mobile device policies (e.g., Intune, Workspace ONE, Jamf, Google MDM).

family_questions.label: External System Connections
family_questions.description: Inventory of external systems, terms of use, and information-sharing controls.

questions.label: External system connection inventory location
questions.help: Where the inventory of external connections is maintained (e.g., 'Boundary diagram in SSP §4.2 + ISA register in Confluence').

questions.label: Terms-of-use mechanism
questions.help: How users acknowledge terms of use (banner / login click-through / signed AUP). References AC-8 (System Use Notification).

questions.label: Information-sharing controls
questions.help: How information shared with external parties is controlled (DLP, watermarking, attribute-based release, ISA scope).

family_questions.label: Identity Populations & Scopes
family_questions.description: Numerical and categorical scope of who accesses this system.

questions.label: Total account count (approximate)
questions.help: Order of magnitude is fine (e.g., '~250 active accounts').

questions.label: Privileged account count
questions.help: Number of privileged / administrative accounts.

questions.label: External (non-employee) account count
questions.help: Contractor / partner / federated user counts.

questions.label: Service / machine account count
questions.help: Non-human accounts used by automation, applications, or services.

family_questions.label: Account Review & Recertification
family_questions.description: Cadence and process for reviewing account inventories and privilege assignments.

questions.label: Dormant-account threshold
questions.help: Inactivity duration that triggers disable / removal review (e.g., '30 days for privileged; 90 days for standard').

questions.label: Privilege recertification process
questions.help: How role / privilege owners review and re-attest their members. Tooling and cadence.

questions.label: Evidence-of-review storage location
questions.help: Where the signed / completed review records are stored.

family_questions.label: Access Control Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate AC control effectiveness over time.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: Mean time to deprovision (MTTD) on departure

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the AC control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.1').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for AC findings
questions.help: Convention for AC-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-AC-').

questions.label: Audit-log correlation (AU-2 / AU-12)
questions.help: How authentication / access events are captured for the audit family. Specify SIEM index, log sources, retention.

questions.label: IA family interaction
questions.help: AC depends on IA (Identification and Authentication) for the underlying identity proofing and authenticator strength. Reference how the two plans interact.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying AC continuous monitoring (account reviews, privileged-access metrics) to the broader ConMon plan.

prompts: Enumerate the account types in scope (individual, group, system, application, guest, anonymous, temporary, emergency).
Identify the account managers (role) for each account type.
State the conditions for group / role membership.
Document approvals required for new account creation and modification.
Describe the monitoring of account usage (logs, anomaly detection).
Address dormant-account detection and disabling — see §6.1 for cadence.
Reference the AC-2 enhancements selected (especially AC-2(1) automated mgmt, AC-2(3) disable inactive, AC-2(4) audit, AC-2(12) account monitoring atypical usage).

extra_fields.label: Account manager role
extra_fields.help: Role responsible for account administration (e.g., 'Identity Operations team').

extra_fields.label: Account-creation approvals
extra_fields.help: Who must approve a new account by type. Supervisor + ISSO is common for privileged.

extra_fields.label: Account monitoring mechanism
extra_fields.help: How account usage is monitored (SIEM rules, UEBA, manual review).

prompts: State the access enforcement model (matches §4.3 — RBAC / ABAC / hybrid).
Identify the policy decision point (PDP) and policy enforcement points (PEPs) — see §4.3.
For RBAC: describe the role catalog and how new roles are authorized.
For ABAC: describe the attribute set, attribute sources, and refresh cadence.
Address bypass mechanisms (none / break-glass) and their controls.
evidence_suggestions: PDP configuration export (IAM policies, OPA bundle, etc.)

extra_fields.label: Enforcement model details
extra_fields.help: Specifics of the model in use, including any application-specific policy engines.

extra_fields.label: Break-glass / emergency access
extra_fields.help: Whether break-glass is allowed; if so, who can invoke, what's logged, retroactive review window.

prompts: Identify the conflict-of-interest role pairs that must be enforced as separate.
Describe how separation is technically enforced (IAM policies, role-incompatibility rules).
Address the review cadence to detect SoD violations (someone holding incompatible roles).
Cross-reference AC-6 (Least Privilege) and AC-2(7) (Privileged User Accounts).
evidence_suggestions: Sample SoD violation report (zero violations preferred)
IAM rule preventing incompatible role assignment

extra_fields.label: Conflict-of-interest role pairs
extra_fields.help: Pairs of roles that must not be held by the same individual (e.g., 'Auditor / Production Deploy', 'AppDev / Production DBA').

extra_fields.label: Technical enforcement
extra_fields.help: How the conflict is prevented at policy assignment time, plus periodic detection of any drift.

prompts: Describe how access is granted at the minimum necessary level for each role.
Identify all privileged roles and their justified scope.
Address just-in-time elevation (AC-6(2)) — see §4.4 for the JIT approach.
Document privilege recertification — see §6.1.
Reference AC-2(7), AC-5, and AU-9(4) (audit log access restrictions).

extra_fields.label: Privileged roles inventory
extra_fields.help: Each privileged role in the system, with a one-line scope. Suggestions are common picks; customize.

extra_fields.label: JIT elevation mechanism
extra_fields.help: How standing privileges are minimized via time-bound elevation. References AC-6(2) and §4.4.

prompts: State the unsuccessful-logon threshold (count over period).
State the lockout duration / behavior (account lock vs delay vs admin reset).
Document the account-recovery / unlock process.
Address whether the threshold differs for privileged vs standard accounts.
evidence_suggestions: IAM / OS authentication policy export showing the threshold

extra_fields.label: Account-recovery process
extra_fields.help: Steps an end user takes to recover from lockout, including identity verification.

prompts: State the idle period that triggers session lock.
Describe the lock mechanism (OS screen lock, application logout, both).
Address re-authentication requirements after lock (password, MFA, biometric).
Document any per-role variation (privileged users may have shorter timeouts).
evidence_suggestions: GPO / Intune / MDM policy export showing idle timeout
Sample audit log showing lock event

extra_fields.label: Re-authentication requirement
extra_fields.help: What's required to unlock (password / PIN / MFA / biometric).

prompts: Describe the remote-access mechanisms in use — see §4.6.
State the authentication requirements for remote access (MFA, certificate-based, hardware token).
Address split-tunneling — whether allowed, and if so under what conditions.
Document the monitoring of remote-access sessions (logging, anomaly detection).
Reference AC-17(2) (cryptographic protection), AC-17(3) (managed access control points), AC-17(4) (privileged commands and access).

extra_fields.label: Remote-access mechanisms
extra_fields.help: VPN client, ZTNA, bastion host, SSH jump host, etc.

extra_fields.label: MFA requirement for remote access
options: Required after first day / new device

prompts: Identify the mobile-device populations served (corp-owned vs BYOD) — see §4.6.
State the MDM / MAM tooling and the policies enforced.
Address encryption requirements for data at rest on mobile devices.
Document the wipe / containerization approach for lost or stolen devices.
Reference AC-19(5) (full device or container encryption).
evidence_suggestions: MDM policy export (Intune / Workspace ONE / Jamf)

extra_fields.label: Mobile encryption-at-rest approach
extra_fields.help: Full-device, container-only, or app-level. Cite AC-19(5) and SC-28 alignment.

glossary.definition: The selective restriction of access to a place or resource. AC controls determine which subjects (users, processes) may perform which actions on which objects.
A representation of an authorized user, group, system, or process within an information system, with associated identifiers, credentials, attributes, and authorizations.
An access-control model where decisions are made by evaluating attributes of the subject, object, action, and environment against a policy.
Verifying the identity of a user, process, or device, typically as a prerequisite to allowing access.
Per NIST SP 800-63B, a measure of the strength of authentication (AAL1 single-factor, AAL2 multi-factor, AAL3 hardware-bound multi-factor).
Granting or denying specific privileges (rights to use resources) based on an authenticated identity's attributes and the access policy.
Emergency access mechanism that grants elevated privileges outside the normal workflow for time-critical incident response, with mandatory retroactive review.
An arrangement allowing identities from one trust domain to be accepted by another, typically via SAML or OIDC.
Per NIST SP 800-63A, a measure of the rigor with which a real-world identity is bound to an account (IAL1 self-asserted, IAL2 verified evidence, IAL3 in-person with biometric).
The three principal events in an account lifecycle: account creation when a person joins, modification on role change, and removal on departure.
An access-management practice where elevated privileges are granted on demand for a bounded time period and automatically revoked on expiration.
The principle of granting users only the minimum access necessary to perform their assigned duties.
Authentication using at least two factors from distinct categories (something you know, have, or are).
A principle stating that access to information should be limited to those who require it to perform official duties.
The system component that evaluates access requests against access-control policy and produces a permit or deny decision.
The system component that intercepts access requests and enforces the PDP's decision (e.g., a load balancer, API gateway, or OS-level access check).
An account with permissions beyond those of a standard user, such as the ability to modify configurations, access security-relevant data, or grant access to others.
A category of cybersecurity tooling and processes that manage and monitor privileged accounts and sessions.
An access-control model where permissions are associated with roles, and users are assigned to one or more roles.
Distributing tasks and associated privileges among multiple individuals so no single person can compromise a process or system.
A non-human account used by automation, applications, or services. Subject to additional rotation and isolation requirements.
An active interaction between a user (or process) and the system, typically authenticated and bounded by login and logout events.
Temporary suspension of an active session that requires re-authentication to resume, while preserving session state.
The conclusive ending of a session that requires full re-authentication and creation of a new session to resume.
An access model that assumes no implicit trust based on network location and continuously evaluates trust at every access decision. Per NIST SP 800-207.
